m1 = oldest month, m6 = most recent. Poisson draw around a customer baseline: higher for active members and customers with 2 products, lower with age, slightly higher for mobile-preferring customers. 70% of churners (10% of retained customers) get a gradual decline that starts in month 3 or 4 and reaches a drop of 25-65% (churners) or 15-45% (retained) in month 6.

Count x average ticket x monthly jitter. Average ticket is log-normal (sigma 0.45) around 35 + 0.00045*salary + 0.00012*balance, giving right-skewed spending. RAW table contains defects (negative reversals, x20 entry errors).

Negative-binomial draw (over-dispersed). Higher for active and mobile-preferring customers, lower with age; scaled down by the month-6 decline factor. RAW table has ~1.5% missing (customers without app tracking).

Dirichlet draw. Younger customers: mobile-heavy; older customers: branch- and ATM-heavy.
